judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard AIA integration and precedence language; 'other documents listed in this Agreement' is a general reference but the operative rule (this Agreement governs inconsistencies) is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement declares itself paramount over 'the other Contract Documents,' yet the First Addendum and Supplementary Conditions—enumerated as Addenda in 15.1.6—expressly revise Agreement paragraphs (Art. 2, 4.1, 4.3, 8.1.8, 12.2.2), a tension only partly cured by 15.1.1 [Revision]. That is a real whole-instrument question about which text prevails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, standard scope clause; 'except to the extent specifically indicated ... to be the responsibility of others' is definite enough on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum contains an 'Article 2 [Revised]' that restates and expands this clause, so the two versions coexist in the enumerated Contract Documents. Otherwise it fits A201 1.1.3 and 3.1.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fill-in reads 'Approximately the Fifteenth of July'—'approximately' leaves the commencement date, from which the Contract Time runs, indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The First Addendum 4.1 [Revised] fixes commencement at July 15, 2002 'pending approval of permits,' which both supersedes and further conditions this date; 4.2 and A201 8.1.2 depend on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence tying Contract Time to the date of commencement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1, A201 8.1.1 and 8.1.2; only indirectly affected by the uncertainty in the commencement date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The completion period is a partly blank fill-in ('five hundred ___ calendar days ... or as follows'), leaving the duration on the face of the form uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 4.3 [Revised] substitutes a fixed date of November 30, 2003, and the new 4.4 bonus keys off 'the established date of Substantial Completion,' so which measure governs is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Contract Sum as Cost of the Work plus Fee, but with a lump-sum fee and no stated ceiling the payment obligation's outer limit turns on what 'the Cost of the Work as defined in Article 7' captures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 9.1.1 says the Contract Sum 'is stated in the Agreement,' yet no sum is stated and 5.2.1's guaranteed maximum is 'N/A'; the progress-payment machinery in 12.1.5-12.1.7 allocates a Guaranteed Maximum Price that does not exist. That is a genuine internal incoherence about how much the Owner owes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee is a bare lump sum ($380,000) with the form's instruction to 'describe the method of adjustment ... for changes in the Work' left unanswered, so whether the fee is fixed regardless of scope is open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12.1.7.3 and 13.2.2 compute the fee by ratio to 'a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work,' an estimate the contract nowhere fixes because the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A'; 6.4 supplies only an 'equitable' adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guaranteed maximum is filled in as 'N/A Dollars ($ N/A)' while the same paragraph says costs exceeding the Guaranteed Maximum Price are borne by the Contractor without reimbursement—an operative sentence with no operative number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Numerous provisions presuppose a real GMP: 8.1.8, 10.2, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7.1-.2, 12.2.5, 13.2 and 13.4 all measure rights by it. With 5.2.1 blanked out, those provisions cannot be harmonised, which is classic whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank fill-in for alternates; nothing is stated, so there is little text to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It recites that the GMP is 'based on' alternates when 5.2.1 states no GMP, a minor extension of the same incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Heading with a blank; no substantive terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 4.3.9 provides for equitable adjustment of 'unit prices ... stated in the Contract Documents,' which here are absent; the mismatch is trivial because the clause says 'if any.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blank allowance schedule with only the form's instruction; nothing to interpret.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.8 elaborately governs allowances 'stated in the Contract Documents,' and none are stated, but 'if any' resolves the gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Blank list of assumptions; no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties to a GMP that is 'N/A' in 5.2.1, but as a blank it creates no independent conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonably inferable' development versus 'such things as changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality' is an open-ended general/specific formulation whose boundary is a familiar battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes the Contractor priced further development into a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves as 'N/A,' and First Addendum 6.5 substitutes a fast-track Preliminary Budget/Change Order procedure for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple cross-reference to A201 7.3.3 methods; the permissive 'may' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adjusts a Guaranteed Maximum Price that does not exist under 5.2.1, and 6.5 of the Addendum prescribes Change Orders adjusting the 'Contract Sum' instead.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed but internally consistent instruction on the meaning of 'cost' and 'fee' in subcontract adjustments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Squares with 6.3, 10.3 and A201 7.3.3; the carve-out for cost-plus subcontracts matches 10.3's consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines 'fee' by reference to 'the Contractor's Fee as defined in Subparagraph 5.1.1,' but the Fee is stated in 5.1.2—an apparent cross-reference slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definitional bridge to A201 7.3.3/7.3.6 works, but it again operates on a Guaranteed Maximum Price that 5.2.1 leaves blank.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial inequity' and 'equitably adjusted' are vague standards, and the clause refers to adjustment provisions 'in Paragraph 5.1' that the parties never filled in.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs that the Guaranteed Maximum Price 'shall be adjusted accordingly' when 5.2.1 sets none; 13.4 also relies on this paragraph for the meaning of 'profit.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs necessarily incurred ... in the proper performance' and 'rates not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project' are open-textured limits that invite argument about particular charges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C's flat 5% payroll add-on for hand tools and Exhibit D's 1% insurance formula are not costs 'necessarily incurred' at 'standard rates,' and Article 8 excludes anything not expressly described in Article 7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain reimbursement item for wages of workers directly employed at the site.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B sets scheduled 'Base Rate' billing figures by position, which may exceed actual wages and sit uneasily with 7.1's 'rates not higher than the standard paid at the place of the Project.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement depends on personnel being 'stationed at the site with the Owner's approval,' and the bracketed cross-reference to Article 14 identification was never completed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.1 excludes principal-office personnel 'except as may be provided in Article 14,' which is blank, and Addendum 8.1.8 declares the Fee to cover senior management and administrative support.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Confined to time actually 'required for the Work'; the limitation is expressed clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 sweeps estimating/project purchasing costs and administrative support into the Fee, which overlaps the expediting personnel described here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Customary benefits such as sick leave, medical and health benefits, holidays, vacations and pensions' is an illustrative list whose reach could be argued, though the tie to included wages is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.2.1-7.2.3 and with Exhibit D's separate treatment of the excise tax; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward materials-cost item.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with 12.1.7.2 and A201 9.3.2 on stored materials; nothing inconsistent found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable waste and spoilage' is a soft boundary, but the ownership and credit mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with 9.1/9.2 crediting sale proceeds to the Owner; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Hand tools not customarily owned by construction workers' and 'fully consumed' are the kind of phrases parties fight over when auditing a cost-plus job.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C states the opposite result—hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor'—while simultaneously adding a flat 5% of payroll for the same tools; that cannot be squared with reimbursement under 7.5.1 and the Article 8 exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allows rental charges for equipment 'whether rented from the Contractor or others,' subject to Owner approval of rates and quantities; the self-rental permission is clear if unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's Equipment Rate Sheet and Exhibit C's statement that rates 'are based upon standard rates paid at the place of the Project' set fixed self-rental rates that must be reconciled with 7.1's rate cap and 8.1.5's exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line reimbursable item; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.15 cleaning up; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable petty cash expenses of the site office' is a soft limit but a minor one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against 8.1.2's exclusion of principal-office expenses, which the site-office qualifier addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of the reasonable expenses ... incurred while travelling in discharge of duties connected with the Work' is qualitative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8's list of Fee-covered items does not clearly cover travel, so the two can be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on advance Owner approval and a mutually acceptable location; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches 12.1.7.2 and A201 9.3.2 and 11.4.1.4 on off-site storage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'That portion of insurance and bond premiums that can be directly attributed to this Contract' turns on an attribution standard that the clause does not define.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D replaces attribution with a flat 1% of labour and subcontractor costs for general liability premiums, a formula that need not correspond to premiums 'directly attributed' to this Contract.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sales, use or similar taxes related to the Work—clear category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D applies the Hawaii general excise tax to all direct costs except subcontract costs and defines 'Subcontract' costs to include listed vendor categories, an overlay that must be read with this item and with A201 3.6.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limited to permits the Contractor 'is required by the Contract Documents to pay'; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.7.1 makes the Contractor secure and pay for the building permit, and 2.2.2 puts easements and assessments on the Owner; the allocation is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Carve-outs are expressed by cross-reference and are internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches A201 13.5.3 (cost of retesting borne by Contractor) and 7.7.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully carved provision; the exclusion of legal defence costs from the Fee calculation is stated expressly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says such costs are not 'subject to the Guaranteed Maximum Price' when 5.2.1 sets none, and it must be read with A201 3.17.1 on royalties and infringement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single reimbursable item, unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 pushes main-office accounting and administrative expenses into the Fee, but data processing 'related to the Work' remains distinguishable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility,' which is qualitative but defined by the Contract Documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 8.1.6 and 7.7.3; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes costs 'arising from disputes between the Owner and Contractor' and requires prior written approval not unreasonably withheld; the categories are stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads together with A201 4.5/4.6 dispute machinery and Supplementary Condition 11.6 on insurance-failure costs; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Keyed to the Contractor's 'standard personnel policy' and Owner approval; the external policy is unspecified but the approval requirement controls.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.1.1's office-salary exclusion; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open catch-all ('other costs') redeemed only by the advance-written-approval condition, which is the sort of general-versus-specific residue courts examine.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1.7 excludes 'any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7,' so whether 7.7.1 lets approved costs escape that exclusion is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cross-references A201 10.6 for emergencies; the standard is externally supplied and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 7.7.2 [Revision] adds conditions excluding emergencies caused by the Contractor or preventable by timely notice, so two versions of the same subparagraph sit in the Contract Documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Negligence or failure to fulfill a specific responsibility' and the insurance-recovery proviso are qualitative but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: First Addendum 7.7.3 [Revision] restates this subparagraph with an added proviso about the Contractor's failure to maintain insurance; the earlier text remains printed in the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bare introductory line to the exclusion list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Introduces exclusions that are modified by Addendum 8.1.8; on its own it creates no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception 'or as may be provided in Article 14' points to a paragraph the parties left blank, leaving the exclusion's boundary uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 8.1.8 puts senior management, executives and administrative support squarely inside the Fee, while 7.2.2 allows site-stationed supervisory salaries; the three must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple exclusion of principal-office expenses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps Addendum 8.1.8's enumeration of main-office overhead covered by the Fee, which is complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overhead and general expenses' is an accounting phrase of uncertain scope, qualified only by 'except as may be expressly included in Article 7.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C's 5% payroll add-on and Addendum 8.1.8 both allocate overhead-type items, so what remains excluded here is a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Exclusion with a single, precise cross-reference exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A's rate sheet and Exhibit C's rental-rate paragraph set the terms on which Contractor-owned equipment is charged, which must be squared with this exclusion and 7.5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long negligence exclusion with a stated exception; qualitative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads with 7.7.3 and its Addendum revision; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any cost not specifically and expressly described in Article 7' is an expressio unius rule sitting against Article 7's own open-ended 7.7.1, so the closure it claims is not complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibits C and D add charging mechanics (5% hand-tool add-on, 1% insurance rate, excise tax treatment) that are not 'specifically and expressly described in Article 7,' creating a direct tension with this exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is expressed in terms of a Guaranteed Maximum Price, a figure this contract never supplies, so the sentence has no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.2.1 fills the guaranteed maximum in as 'N/A' and Addendum 8.1.8 replaces this subparagraph with a Fee-coverage provision; the exclusion cannot operate as written.
